question: Does fine-tuning nli-deberta-v3-xsmall on GitHub issue->PR pairs from held-out repos lift U2 (error resolved?) above the best prior arm?
machine_load_note: Scoring and training ran beside a CPU-bound LongMemEval benchmark (1-minute load 13-19 on 16 threads). Latencies below are recorded but not comparable to other runs.

U1.question: Does the NEW statement replace, update, or contradict the OLD statement, so that the OLD statement is no longer current?

U2.question: Does the LATER note show that the ERROR has actually been fixed?

u2_test_paired_vs_base.bootstrap: 2000 cluster resamples, shared by every arm (paired)

u2_test_paired_vs_laya.bootstrap: 2000 cluster resamples, shared by every arm (paired)

verdict.summary: Large, stable gain over the untuned base; ahead of the best prior arm (Laya typed-decisions) by about 0.10 AUROC, but that difference is not established at 95% on this test set.
verdict.vs_base: paired AUROC gain +0.18 to +0.19 per seed; every cluster-bootstrap 95% interval excludes 0
verdict.vs_laya: paired gain +0.10 to +0.11 per seed; 95% intervals from about -0.02 to +0.23, one of three excludes 0
verdict.sibling_repo_ablation: dropping the test repos' sibling projects from training leaves U2 AUROC unchanged
verdict.status_negatives: fixed vs same-bug-not-fixed negatives (n=15 negatives) rises from 0.62 (base) to 0.77-0.80
verdict.u1_side_effect: U1 AUROC falls from 0.745 to about 0.68: the tuned model is U2-only, never a U1 judge
verdict.operating_point: FPR at the train-fit threshold is 0.07-0.12 on test, above the 0.05 target; a 29.12b suggestion list ranks top-3 and never auto-resolves, so it relies on ranking, not on this threshold
verdict.limits: 111 test rows in 56 dependent clusters; 77% of test negatives are fixes for another bug; the Axil subset has 15 test rows. Not for README/docs/CLI (see the typed-decisions README numbers policy).
